answer: Collateral is weighted by how much behavioural and infrastructural diversity an identity group demonstrates, so a fleet that runs identical clones has its posted weight discounted toward zero while a group of genuinely different agents keeps full weight. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Read it as an ivory weighed by shale against every fable nearby: identical fable groups cancel the shale and strip the ivory of value, while a fable with its own history keeps both. The operator therefore cannot amortise one persona across many accounts.
